title: The Cathedral of Flesh
summary: The living church of the Tzimisce.

claims.text: The Tzimisce Yorak, set to guard a germ of the Antediluvian's mind, built a church-fortress sculpted from the bodies of peasants, slaves, rivals and beasts.
It first stood in Yorak's domain near the Carpathians; tonight no one knows where it is, and some say it has budded copies or is now the Antediluvian's own body.

title: The Vampire Club
summary: An Anarch Elysium in San Francisco.

claims.text: Set in the beached hull of a bankrupt millionaire's yacht, it is a prize of the Anarch Free State, and Kindred of every faction treat it as Elysium.

title: Catedral da Se
summary: The Sabbat's council in Sao Paulo.

claims.text: A council meets each year in the crypts beneath the cathedral to observe and set down the Sabbat's ritae; Archbishops, Bishops and Prisci attend by invitation only.
The Archbishop of Sao Paulo also hosts deliberative diets of the Sect's leaders.

title: Red Sisters Midnight
summary: A wandering market of Kindred contraband.

claims.text: In domains of harsh Princes the market brokers forbidden goods such as relics of undead saints and banned Thaumaturgy, items with no worldly price.
Ravnos of the Phuri Dae bloodline run it.
The tunnels cut into the Anatolian mountains hid early Christians and also fugitive vampires of the Clan of Death that the Giovanni overthrew.

title: Highgate Cemetery
summary: A London graveyard with a dark name.

claims.text: Opened in the mid-19th century, Highgate has always had ties to the supernatural, including talk of a Vampire of Highgate in the 1970s and 1980s.
A panopticon prison for criminals and enemies of the ruling party, where starvation, torture and death awaited the condemned.

title: Gaslamp
summary: San Diego in the Anarch Free State.

claims.text: No domain of the West Coast Anarch Free State has suffered more; the Free State has lost ground to a domain that rejoined the Camarilla and another overthrown by the Kindred of the East.

title: Lodin's Boardroom
summary: The sealed haven of a dead Prince.

claims.text: Chicago's Prince Lodin called a Blood Hunt on the werewolves in the mid-1990s and died in the Lupine rampage, along with half the city's Kindred.

The haven is said to hold the Roll of the Damned, listing every Kindred since Caine, and a 13th century amulet bearing the True Name of the Methuselah Menele, though some think these rumours are bait.
Romans who sacked Carthage told of human sacrifice and children thrown to the flames; those who speak Moloch's tongue are said to breed nightmares and desecration.
Byzantium's Dream, a Cainite utopia of learning led by lost Methuselahs, fell through betrayal, finally of its own champion, the Patriarch.
A copy of the medieval Hagia Sophia is said to lie beneath the real one; scholars rank it with the Library of Alexandria for history and hints of the Damned's fate.
The first club opened in Chicago in the early 1990s, where Kindred fed on mortals drawn to the vampire scene; tonight it is a nomadic party moving across North America.
Vienna holds Clan Tremere's most advanced chantry, the unquestioned centre of its political and Thaumaturgical power.
The Clan's ancestral home, where assassins train and sorcerers keep their lore, and where the Old Man under the mountain directs the Clan.
A 19th century ossuary of more than six million dead, partly open to the public, with hidden rooms and tunnels that Kindred use.

title: Dr. Netchurch's Laboratory
summary: A Malkavian science lab in Lowell.

claims.text: The Malkavian bioeschatologist Douglas Netchurch leads the posthumous sciences, studying how vampires react to modern stimuli.
On Vesteroy the Kindred rule openly, and their few mortal thralls exist only to serve and feed them, perhaps close to the First City's terror.

title: The Abbey of the Sacred Crown
summary: Where the Convention of Thorns was held.

claims.text: In this modest monastery near the village of Thorns, the young Camarilla ended the Anarch Revolt and the Assamites accepted the curse that checked their diablerie.
The Ventrue and Toreador Princes of Scandinavia long ignored the Anarch threat, blaming the violence on refugees fleeing Baba Yaga in Russia.
Once one of the Clan's largest spawning pits, the island held nearly enough Nosferatu to rival the Giovanni; now it is a wretched, half-empty warren.
Werewolves and mages of Dallas once fought over the park as a store of mystic energy.
Cordoned off since the Turkish invasion of 1974, Varosha is frozen in time, its shops still hung with clothes untouched for decades.
The plantation-owning Chase family bought the churchyard vault in the early 19th century; it had been used only once before.
